one_liner: Single-file C11 planar geometry library whose indexed point-in-polygon and intersects tests beat GEOS PreparedGeometry by about 1.1-2.7x.
what_it_does: TG implements the OGC Simple Features types (Point through GeometryCollection), the binary predicates (intersects, contains, within, covers, coveredby, touches, equals, disjoint) and readers/writers for GeoJSON, WKT, WKB, hex WKB and GeoBIN. It targets real-time geofencing and monitoring: build a polygon once, then test millions of points or segments against it. The API is a plain C, purely functional one (tg_geom_intersects_xy(), tg_parse_wkt_ix(), tg_ring_new_ix() and so on) and is not GEOS-compatible; the separate tgx project bridges TG and GEOS geometries. Overlay, buffering, convex hull, Voronoi and similar GIS algorithms are explicit non-goals.
how_it_is_fast: Point-in-polygon is ray casting, accelerated by two segment indexes built at ring construction. Natural indexing is a flat, multi-level R-tree-like array of branch MBRs whose leaf level is the ring's own segment array in its original order (default spread 16), so the index adds about 7% memory and builds in one pass; by default its rectangles are 32-bit floats rounded outward. YStripes splits the y-range into hash-bucket-like stripes (count from a Polsby-Popper compactness score times segment count, minimum 32), each listing the segments it crosses, which gives O(1) lookup of the segments a horizontal ray can hit. Multi-geometries get a Hilbert-curve-ordered index over their members, clones are O(1) via atomic reference counting, and min/max use single minsd/maxsd instructions on x86-64 to avoid branches.
when_to_use: Geofencing or stream filtering: many points tested against a fixed set of large polygons (10^3-10^5 vertices), where TG Natural gave 10-22M ops/s on one core for the real-world state and country outlines in the author's runs
Polygons that are created or reloaded often: Natural index builds in tens of microseconds (Brazil, 39,914 points: 53 us vs 2,060 us for a GEOS prepared geometry) and uses about 4.5x less memory
Peak point-in-polygon throughput on a long-lived polygon: index it with TG_YSTRIPES (about 1.5-2.7x GEOS prepared on the larger shapes) and keep Natural for other predicates
Fast WKB/GeoJSON/WKT ingestion in C or C++ (Brazil WKB read 28,320 vs GEOS 3,150 ops/s in the same run)
Embedding a small, dependency-free geometry core in C/C++ services or WebAssembly builds
when_not_to_use: You need overlay (union/intersection/difference), buffering, simplification, convex hull, Voronoi, DE-9IM relate matrices or validity repair: TG does not implement them; use GEOS
Geographic (lon/lat on the sphere) semantics: TG is planar Cartesian only, so polygons crossing the antimeridian or spanning large areas need your own handling

Edge-case OGC semantics on collections and multilinestrings: as of 2026-10-01, issues #29 (covers over multiple components) and #30 (mod-2 boundary rule) are open, and #20 and #24 were only fixed in September 2026
Input that may be invalid: rings are defined as closed and non-self-intersecting, but tg.c does not check self-intersection, so bad input gives undefined predicate answers
Highly irregular random-shaped polygons where you want YStripes: on the Random-100 and Random-1000 tests it was slower than Natural, and it costs about 20x Natural's build time

integration.dependencies: none (tg.c and tg.h; C standard library, stdatomic.h unless TG_NOATOMICS is defined)
integration.min_toolchain: C11 compiler; MSVC builds were fixed in September 2026 (issue #15, GCC builtins)
integration.platforms: Portable C: x86-64 (inline minsd/maxsd asm under GCC/Clang), aarch64, WebAssembly via Emscripten; big-endian WKB (#18) and ARMv7 alignment (#12) fixed in 2025, wasm32/ILP32 struct-layout bug (#26) closed 2026-09-24
integration.thread_safety: Library functions are documented as thread-safe and reentrant, with atomic reference counts for shared geometries. The tg_env_set_* globals (allocator, default index, spread) must be called once at startup before any other tg_* call.

gotchas: tg_geom_contains/within return false for a point on the polygon edge; use tg_geom_covers or tg_geom_intersects when boundary points must count

Arithmetic is plain double with a precision-loss nudge (nexttoward) inside the collinear and raycast tests, not exact or extended-precision predicates; index rectangles are float32 rounded outward unless you build with TG_IXFLOAT64
Constructors clone their inputs by reference count: every tg_*_new/parse/clone/copy needs exactly one free. Upcasting tg_line/tg_ring/tg_poly to tg_geom is free, but downcasting is unsafe
Parsers return an error geometry rather than NULL on bad input; check tg_geom_error() and handle NULL for out-of-memory
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick TG when the job is polygon predicates (point-in-polygon, segment/geometry intersects) against a few large polygons. nanoflann, tidwall/rtree.c and GeoToolbox KdBoxTree index many separate points or boxes and pair well with TG as a first-stage filter, while Manifold, MeshLib and trueform are 3D mesh libraries for a different problem.
verified_claims_summary: The author's tests/bench.c (GEOS_BENCH=1) times 10K random points within each polygon's MBR plus 10%, best of 10 runs, on an AMD Ryzen 9 5950X with gcc 11.4.0 -O3 against GEOS 3.12.0 built from source. On Brazil (39,914 points), TG YStripes reaches 15.17M ops/s and Natural 10.14M against GEOS prepared at 7.89M and unprepared at 29.7K; on Texas, YStripes reaches 22.45M against 9.87M. Across all 13 PIP polygons Natural is 1.08-2.5x and YStripes 1.35-2.7x GEOS prepared (derived from page data), with identical hit counts. The GEOS loop calls the generic GEOSPreparedIntersects_r on prebuilt point geometries, while TG calls its point-specialised tg_poly_intersects_point, so part of the gap is per-call overhead rather than the index.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-26, about 676 stars, MIT), with a stream of predicate-correctness fixes from an outside contributor in September 2026; the library is one tg.c plus tg.h, so vendoring a current commit is easy.
